note: License policy for the third-party components compiled into ./cmd/lit — Go modules AND the statically-linked native C libraries (ICU, zstd, musl, compiler-rt; see native.go). Every allowed_licenses entry except MPL-2.0 is a permissive license with no copyleft obligation that conflicts with lit's MIT 'free for any purpose' guarantee; MPL-2.0 (file-level copyleft) is the known residual, kept until links-licensing-c0ce.9 tightens the allowlist. A component whose license (per tools/licenses' classifier for Go modules, or the curated license in native.go for native libs) is not in allowed_licenses must appear in module_exceptions with a reason, or the CI license-policy gate (`go run ./tools/licenses -check`, and TestDependencyLicensesArePermitted) fails. Matching is by EXACT STRING, never by parsing SPDX: an entry may be a single identifier or a whole expression (compiler-rt's 'MIT AND Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception' is the only expression today), so a semantically identical rewording — reordered arms, a different spacing — is a different string and fails the gate with a misleading non-allowlisted-license message. Copy an expression exactly as native.go states it. The corollary of never parsing is that an expression entry allowlists the COMBINATION without the gate ever vetting its arms: 'MIT AND Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception' is here because a human confirmed both arms are permissive, not because anything checked. So every AND-arm of an expression added here must have its base identifier independently present in this list (a WITH-exception only widens the grant, it never narrows it), and an OR must never appear at all — lit resolves a dual license to the elected arm before it reaches policy, recording it as a single identifier plus acknowledgement 'concluded' (see zstd in native.go), so an OR entry in this file means an election went unmade. Both are reader-enforced today; links-licensing-c0ce.9 moves them into the gate. Expression entries are also inert in the module-graph audit, whose per-file classifications are always single identifiers. This is the single committed policy file; edit it to accept a new license class (allowed_licenses) or to record a per-module, human-verified exception (module_exceptions). See links-supply-chain-w6m9.3 and w6m9.4.
